MMM.name: 3M
MMM.numbers_line: EPS $2.50 vs $2.38 est (beat, +12%); revenue $6.60B vs $6.61B est (in line), organic growth +3.3%; operating margin 26.2% (+110bp), free cash flow $1.2B. The stock was up ~6% at midday.
MMM.guidance: Full-year EPS raised to $9.10–9.15 on the new ex-amortisation basis (from $8.95–9.10); organic growth above 3.5% with Q4 just over 4%; margin ~24.6%; free cash flow ~$4.8B. Oil-driven cost inflation now $185M (from $150–175M), fully offset by price. 2027 framework: growth in line with the ~4% second-half exit rate, margin above the 25.4% investor-day target, incrementals near 40%, stranded costs down to $50M.
call_said: The data-centre story: an 8-K last night issued Amazon a warrant for up to 3.2M shares (~0.6%) that vests on $6B of cumulative optical-connectivity and data-centre sales over seven years; a contract-manufacturing deal and 4.7% stake in GSEO to scale the Expanded Beam Optical connector; Microsoft already deploying it in Azure; the multi-source agreement has grown from 17 to 63 members. EBO is ~$40M this year, $80–100M next, against a ~$2B 2028 addressable market; total data-centre revenue ~$700M this year from ~$550M.

Demand: orders up ~7% and backlog up 18%, US and Canada +7% ('the highest we have seen since the pandemic'), industrials double digits. The weak spots are consumer electronics (down mid-teens on LCD displays and China OEMs), China down high single digits, auto builds down modestly, US consumer flat with point-of-sale up ~2% against retailer destocking.

Self-help continues: 16 sites closed year to date and 10 more coming, gross margin +230bp, 87 new products in the quarter (+24%) and 350-plus for the year, R&D cycle time down 20% with AI expected to compress it further; a court-appointed mediator is working the AFFF personal-injury litigation.
MMM.quote: "This is a self-help story. We're showing that we can grow organically, even in a choppy macro environment." — Bill Brown
MMM.read_through: A legacy industrial being repriced as a data-centre supplier, and the market paid for it on the day. With FAST and PLD it is the third name this week to put a number on data-centre demand; the consumer-electronics weakness rhymes with TSMC's warning on price-sensitive end markets.

NOC.name: Northrop Grumman
NOC.numbers_line: EPS $7.89 vs $7.18 est (beat, +3% y/y); revenue $11.1B vs $11.1B est (+7%); book-to-bill 1.5×, record backlog $110B (+20%); segment margin 12.1%; adjusted free cash flow $1.8B (+40%, including $371M from selling a B-21 test asset). The stock was up ~5% at midday.
NOC.guidance: Sales $43.75–44.25B held; segment operating income raised to $4.94–5.04B (~11.3% margin); EPS raised by $0.70 (performance plus a lower tax rate); free cash flow $3.1–3.5B held. 2027: sales +5–7% with all four segments growing, margin +10–20bp, capex ~$2.1B (4.5% of sales) for the B-21 acceleration, free cash flow $3.3–3.7B; growth accelerates again in 2028; international sales to double by 2031.
call_said: The franchise programmes: B-21 production acceleration with facilities through 2028, Sentinel cleared for first flight in 2027 with another $2B awarded, $4.6B of restricted awards, 21 Tranche 1 transport-layer satellites launched with ~50 more in six months, Virginia-class Block VI propulsion for $1.4B. The B-21 loss burn-down was $70M against a ~$100M quarterly norm.

New: Northrop is 'actively evaluating strategic alternatives' for its microelectronics and quantum (reciprocal quantum logic) technology, from outside investment to a separation; 'everything is on the table'. Fortitude, a chip 'the size of a grain of rice' with 3× the power and 20× the signal quality of comparable parts, is being built for defence and commercial use.

Munitions: ~$1B of solid-rocket-motor work growing as Northrop becomes a component supplier (motors, fuzes, warheads, nozzles); RAIDR, a 50mm gun-based counter-drone system, drawing allied demand; Talon Blue flew fully autonomously 24 months from design. On the continuing resolution: 'relatively insulated'. About 35% of backlog burns in the next 12 months.
NOC.quote: "Everything is on the table." — Kathy Warden, on the microelectronics and quantum review
NOC.read_through: Defence demand is contracted and accelerating into 2028; the quantum and microelectronics review is a new angle for the quantum names in the universe (IONQ). LMT reports 22 Oct against this backdrop.

RTX.name: RTX
RTX.numbers_line: EPS $2.26 vs $1.78 est (large beat, +33%, of which $0.25 is IEEPA tariff recovery); revenue $25.0B vs $24.1B est (+12% organic); record backlog $340B (+36%) after ~$59B of defence awards (Tomahawk ~$23B, AMRAAM $14B-plus) for a 4.57× book-to-bill; free cash flow $2.1B. The stock was about flat at midday.
RTX.guidance: Raised: sales $97–97.5B (from $95–96B), organic growth 10–11% (from 8–9%); EPS $7.65–7.75 (from $7.10–7.25, $0.25 of the raise is IEEPA); free cash flow $9.0–9.2B (from $8.5–8.75B). Commercial aftermarket now low-double-digit to low-teens growth, defence low double digits. 2027: growth, margin expansion and higher free cash flow, with the powder-metal tailwind (~$500M) roughly offsetting the lost IEEPA refunds and pension drag.
call_said: Airlines are trimming Q4 flying on fuel; Calio's answer was the numbers: aftermarket +16% organic despite RPKs down slightly, GTF MRO output +35%, AOGs stable and expected to fall in Q4, the first GTF Advantage in service at United, retirements low. 'Demand has continued to be resilient. We think it is durable.'

The munitions supercycle is now contracted: ~$70B of multi-year undefinitized contracts (Tomahawk, AMRAAM, SM-6, SM-3 IIA) to take rates up 2–4× over 7–10 years, with downside protections if budgets change. Ron Epstein: 'Nobody can get printed circuit boards' and passives are short because of the AI build-out; Calio called supply chain 'the single biggest enabling factor', 150 new suppliers added in 2025, rocket motors via partnerships not M&A.

Collins margins above 18% ex IEEPA on structural cost cuts; Pratt 'entitled to low-to-mid-teens margins' over time as GTF Advantage and the Hot Section Plus kit cut in; international is 37% of backlog (52% ex the munitions contracts); NDAA right-to-repair provisions flagged; Pratt's president is retiring, Jill Albertelli takes over.
RTX.quote: "You are hitting on the single biggest enabling factor in getting to these enhanced rates… it is absolutely gonna take a change in how we do things with our supply chain." — Chris Calio, on components
RTX.read_through: Two things for the universe: a decade of munitions demand is signed, and the AI build-out is now visibly crowding defence out of circuit boards and passives (VSH, TEL, APH read). The aftermarket is holding against $111 oil for now.

SYF.name: Synchrony Financial
SYF.numbers_line: EPS $2.68 vs $2.42 est (beat); FMP's revenue line ($4.91B actual vs $3.81B est) compares gross interest and fees with a net-revenue estimate, so it is not like for like. Purchase volume ~$50B (+8%, a record third quarter), receivables $103B (+3%), NII $4.8B (+2%), NIM 15.5%, net charge-offs 4.79% (from 5.16%), ROTCE 25.2%, $1.1B of buybacks. The stock was down ~1% at midday.
SYF.guidance: Full-year EPS ~ $9.50, the top of the original $9.10–9.50 range and above the $9.38–9.40 consensus; receivables up mid single digits, charge-offs below 5.5%, RSA within 4–4.5%, Q4 NIM up sequentially, Q4 expense in line with Q3. 2027: the framework 'should' still deliver double-digit EPS growth; deposit betas expected to be higher than last cycle given promotional competition; one more hike in December assumed.
call_said: The CFO listed what the January guide did not know: 'a war in Iran… higher gas prices… inflation accelerating… a rise in the Fed funds rate'. The consumer spent through all of it: spend +8%, fastest among Gen Z and millennials, non-discretionary gas and discount-store spend up double digits, no stress in delinquencies, and the first three weeks of October tracking at the Q3 exit rate. Retailers plan slightly heavier and earlier holiday promotions.

Agentic commerce: an OpenAI collaboration and ChatGPT plug-in, the Personal Agent Protocol with Sierra and Meta, a Stripe integration for CareCredit; Doubles argues agents will favour cards with the best offers, which helps private label, while admitting the risk that agents optimise consumers into revolving less.

Why the stock lagged: the implied Q4 is below the Street on reserve cadence (Walmart OnePay losses coming online, credit actions seasoning), operational losses ran high on idiosyncratic events, technology spend is elevated through next year, and the payment rate at 16.9% is 180bp above pre-pandemic on mix.
SYF.quote: "We began the year with the range of $9.10 to $9.50… which preceded a war in Iran, preceded the higher gas prices that Americans are feeling today, preceded inflation accelerating and preceded a rise in the Fed funds rate." — Brian Wenzel, CFO
SYF.read_through: The credit-card consumer is spending more and paying on time, but the growth is in gas and discount stores. Read for COF (tonight), AXP (23 Oct) and the retailers; higher deposit betas are the same funding story SFNC and USB told.

PGR.name: Progressive
PGR.numbers_line: FMP today: EPS $4.66 vs $4.35 est (beat); revenue $22.3B vs $22.6B est. The Hub's earnings_events row still carries an earlier FMP answer ($1.08 and $7.2B, a monthly figure) that FMP has since corrected: flagged for the data desk.
PGR.guidance: Progressive does not hold a quarterly call (its investor webcast comes later); the transcript watch shows 'waiting'. No guidance to report.
call_said: No stored call. Read with TRV (16 Oct): personal-auto renewal pricing is now slightly negative at Travelers after ~10 rate decreases, and the Marsh index shows commercial pricing down 5%.
PGR.read_through: Personal lines pricing has turned; the reaction (−4.2% on the day, +3.2% since) says the market took the print as the top of the margin cycle, then bought the dip.

STLD.name: Steel Dynamics
STLD.numbers_line: EPS $5.26 vs $5.48 est (miss); revenue $6.51B vs $6.43B est (beat). The call is this morning, 20 Oct; the transcript was not yet in the Hub's table when this was built (watch status 'waiting').
call_said: No stored call. Read with CLF (19 Oct): hot-rolled index up ~$40/t a month, imports 35–40% below pre-tariff, customers 'focused on securing volume than price', and GM's complaint the same morning that steel is at four-year highs.
STLD.read_through: Steel pricing power is intact; the miss on EPS with a beat on revenue reads as cost (scrap, energy) rather than demand. NUE reports 26 Oct.
